topic: The Hidden Mechanics of Light: Origin and Color Dependence of Refraction
target_audience: Undergraduate Physics/Engineering Students or Advanced High School Students

sections.title: Prerequisite: Light as an Electromagnetic Interaction
lecture_lines: Light is an oscillating electromagnetic field moving through space.
Refractive index n is the ratio of speeds c/v.
Changing speed causes path bending, like a runner on sand.
animations: Display an oscillating sine wave (#00FFFF) labeled 'Electromagnetic Field' (#00FFFF).
Introduce the formula 'n = c / v' (#FFFFFF) with labels 'c: Vacuum' (#AAAAAA) and 'v: Medium' (#AAAAAA).
Show a 'light-runner' icon (#FFD700) moving across a grey 'Paved Road' surface.
Animate the runner entering a yellow 'Sand' region (#FFFF00), slowing down and changing angle.
Display a green laser beam (#00FF00) refracting at a glass block boundary to illustrate the macroscopic effect.

sections.title: The Microscopic Origin: The Atomic Dance
lecture_lines: Slowing down is an illusion created by wave superposition.
Incoming waves force electrons to oscillate like springs.
These oscillating electrons radiate their own secondary waves.
Secondary waves interfere with the original driving wave.
The resultant wave appears delayed, moving slower through matter.
animations: Show a row of atoms (#FFFFFF) as circles on [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/springs.svg], representing the Lorentz Oscillator Model.
An incoming light wave (#00FFFF) hits the atoms, making the electrons (#FFFF00) oscillate.
Show the oscillation spreading through the atoms with a slight delay between each.
Visualize secondary EM waves (#00FF00) being emitted by each oscillating electron.
Show the sum of original and secondary waves forming a slower resultant wave (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization: The Phase Velocity
lecture_lines: Driving and induced waves exhibit a relative phase shift.
Rotating phasors represent these electric field components.
Vector addition yields a resultant with a retarded phase.
Permittivity scales the magnitude of the induced response.
Refractive index n depends on the material's relative permittivity.
animations: Display a 'Vacuum Wave' (#00FFFF) as a steady sine wave moving across the upper half of the screen.
Show a 'Medium Wave' (#FFFFFF) below it, shifted to demonstrate a clear phase lag.
Introduce a rotating 'Driving Phasor' (#00FFFF) vector in a circular diagram.
Add an 'Induced Phasor' (#00FF00) from the same origin, lagging by 90 degrees.
Construct the 'Resultant Phasor' (#FFFFFF) via vector addition, showing the final retarded phase.

sections.title: Color Dependence: The Resonance Effect
lecture_lines: Atoms have natural resonant frequencies for electron vibration.
Light closer to resonance interacts more strongly.
Higher frequencies like violet create larger phase lags.
This causes violet light to bend more than red.
This frequency-dependent bending is known as dispersion.
animations: Display a graph of refractive index 'n' vs wavelength 'lambda' (#FFFFFF) showing normal dispersion.
Show a red wave (#FF0000) and a violet wave (#8F00FF) both approaching a row of atoms.
Animate the electrons (#FFFF00) vibrating more intensely in response to the violet wave's frequency.
Show the violet wave experiencing a larger phase lag compared to the red wave.
Visualize violet light bending more than red light when passing through a prism [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg].

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Rainbow and the Mantis Shrimp
lecture_lines: Dispersion creates rainbows as sunlight splits in droplets.
Prisms visualize the full spectrum of visible light.
Mantis shrimp eyes use specialized filters for hyperspectral vision.
animations: Animate a light ray inside a water droplet (#00FFFF) reflecting and refracting to create a rainbow.
Show white light entering a glass prism [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg] and splitting into a visible color spectrum.
